title: Number of Pairs of Interchangeable Rectangles
summary: Given a list of rectangles defined by their width and height, count the number of pairs of rectangles that have the same width-to-height ratio using decimal division.
statement: Given a list of rectangles defined by their width and height, count the number of pairs of rectangles that have the same width-to-height ratio using decimal division.
constraints: rectangles has 1 through 100000 positive width-height pairs, each coordinate at most 100000.
Two rectangles are interchangeable when width/height ratios are equal.
Return the number of unordered interchangeable pairs.
hints: Reduce each ratio to a canonical integer pair to avoid floating-point error.
Divide width and height by their greatest common divisor and count prior equal keys.
For each reduced ratio, add its existing frequency to the answer, then increment it.
Canonical reduction is equal exactly for equal rational ratios, and adding prior frequency counts every unordered pair once when its later rectangle arrives.
editorial: Canonical reduction is equal exactly for equal rational ratios, and adding prior frequency counts every unordered pair once when its later rectangle arrives.
